sections.heading: What it buys
points: Throughput, not latency: one instruction is no faster, but more finish per second.
A k-stage pipeline holds k instructions at once.
Ideal speedup is k; real speedup is less, because of hazards.

sections.heading: The three hazards
points: Structural: two instructions want the same hardware.
Data: an operand is not written back yet. Forwarding often fixes it.
Control: a branch, whose outcome is unknown when the next fetch happens.

sections.heading: Traps the quiz likes
points: The clock period is set by the SLOWEST stage, not the average.
Deeper is not automatically better: branch penalties grow with depth.
Pipeline registers add delay of their own.
